correctness.rationale: For any finite simple bipartite G and matching-covered-vertex concepts (empty matching allowed), shattering S requires separate labelings positive only on S∩L and only on S∩R, which yield vertex-disjoint crossing submatchings saturating S. Conversely any such crossing matching can be thinned to realize every trace; the two Hall inequalities follow. Hence VCdim=ν(G) (choose one endpoint from each maximum-matching edge), K_(a,b) has all supports of size≤min(a,b). On paths P_(5t+1), selecting vertex positions 5j+2,5j+3 gives unique forced outside neighbors; no unselected vertex can join, so facet size2t vs max floor((5t+1)/2). Triangle K3 boundary violates bipartite conclusion. Independent direct trace/matching cut enumeration for P5; inspected exhaustive checker and its boundary logic.
